prompt: Make a short film that opens on one statement as its whole first shot: 'Most dashboards hide where a number came from', with the word 'hide' emphasised. Add a second shot that answers it with a statement of your own. Keep it under 12 seconds. The film is silent: no voice.

Show data/portrait.jpg as a clipping with the caption 'The speaker'. Name a region around the face and push in on it at the word 'face' of the shot's say text. Write two short say sentences for the shot. The film is silent: no voice.
Make a film that reveals a bar or column chart of quarterly signups (Q1 1200, Q2 1850, Q3 2400, Q4 3100), highlights Q4, and says 'Signups grew every quarter'. The film is silent: no voice.

Make a vertical film for Reels in the viral mode with three shots: a hook statement, a number shot counting up to 64%, and an end card whose ask is 'Read the report'. The film is silent: set sound to off.

Make a 15-second narrated explainer in the pro mode with three shots, each with its own spoken line (say), about why a team should keep its data in one file. Do not set a duration on a shot that has a spoken line.

Make a data story film for a company all-hands: support tickets fell from 1,840 in January to 1,310 in February, 960 in March, 720 in April, 610 in May and 540 in June; first-reply time went from 9 hours to 2.5 hours over the same months; the drop started when the help centre search was rebuilt in February. The point: better search, not more staff, cut the queue. It is a pro film in 16:9, 20 to 40 seconds long, and silent (no voice, music or sound). Write your own shot list.

Make a product launch film for Fieldnote, a notes app that works offline. Facts to use: notes sync when the phone is back online, 40 notes open in under a second, it runs on iOS and Android, it costs 3 dollars a month and the first month is free. End with the ask 'Try it at fieldnote.example'. It is a pro film in 16:9, 20 to 40 seconds long, and silent (no voice, music or sound). Write your own shot list.

Make a film that explains how a hash table finds a value, for someone who knows what an array is. Cover: a key goes through a hash function, the result picks a slot, two keys can land in the same slot (a collision), the slot then holds a short list, and a table that gets too full is grown and refilled. Use one worked example through the whole film. It is a pro film in 16:9, 20 to 40 seconds long, and silent (no voice, music or sound). Write your own shot list.

Make a before-and-after film about a checkout redesign: before, 5 screens and 61 percent of carts abandoned; after, 1 screen and 38 percent abandoned; 11 weeks of work by a team of 4. The point: fewer screens, fewer lost carts. Say what changed and what did not (prices, shipping cost). It is a pro film in 16:9, 20 to 40 seconds long, and silent (no voice, music or sound). Write your own shot list.

Make a news-style recap of a week in a city's bike share: Monday 12,400 rides, Tuesday 13,900, Wednesday 9,100 (a storm closed 30 stations), Thursday 14,800, Friday 17,200, Saturday 21,500 (a record), Sunday 16,300. Then one quote from the operations lead, Dana Ortiz: 'We had every bike back by Friday noon.' Close on what happens next: 12 new stations open on the first of the month. It is a pro film in 16:9, 20 to 40 seconds long, and silent (no voice, music or sound). Write your own shot list.
